summary.one_liner: TermaGITchi is a Go CLI (`pets`) that gives each Claude Code agent session a creature in its status line, hashed from the session id, with its mood reflecting how tidy the git worktree is.
summary.what_it_does: It assigns each agent session a creature derived by hashing the session id, so nothing is picked or saved. Each git worktree is shown as a den named after a city, with a flight-code glyph such as "@ DXB". The creature's expression tracks repository hygiene, such as uncommitted files, unpushed commits, and distance behind upstream. `pets install` wires the status line and hooks into detected agents while backing up touched config, and `pets uninstall` reverses it. Users can add external signals: any executable printing key=value can feed penalties or bounds that affect the pet's mood. The README also describes tmux and shell-prompt rendering, plus a `pets render --format=json` output for building custom displays. Claude Code is the only agent the README says was verified end to end; Codex CLI support is described with a caveat about hook trust.
use_cases: tell parallel Claude Code sessions apart in the status line
see git worktree hygiene at a glance
show a terminal pet in tmux or shell prompt
track uncommitted and unpushed changes per worktree
add custom health checks like clippy warnings or coverage to a status display
build a JSON-driven status display for an editor
stack: Claude Code status line and hooks
notable: Creature identity is a hash of the agent session id, so each parallel session has a stable, recognisable creature with 41 species, rarity bands, and shiny variants
Worktrees map to ddens named after 16 cities
Mood reflects git hygiene; custom external signals can be added with simple shell scripts that print key=value
Install backs up config it modifies and leaves other settings alone; uninstall reverses it
Network-free status line path; update checks run only for card, party, and den commands and can be disabled
caveats: Claude Code is the only agent verified end to end according to the README
Codex hooks do nothing until the user explicitly trusts them in Codex, and the binary is required even when using the plugin
Homebrew upgrades may require running `brew trust TevvvB/tap` first
